is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m starting with the workspace contract and the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this task explicitly requires interpreting current multi-wake rollout evidence before changing the target policy. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and will not use or reconstruct the omitted research shelf.

The current parent is a phase-headroom propulsion anchor plus a close/receding bearing reversal. The durable guidance already marks the globally active reversal as a negative result, so I’m now separating the four sampled candidates and their inherited notes to identify which close-gated mechanism actually changed the trajectory—and which merely repeated the upper-boundary failure.

The visual comparison is decisive: all four fish actively propel upstream, but none enters the useful target wake corridor. The plain phase-headroom anchor remains best overall (`3.03L` minimum distance, `0.517` progress); both close-gated reversals fire only near the miss, shave propulsion, and still produce the identical upper hook. The longitudinal sign gate is worse again (`3.45L`, `0.449`). I’m treating those as concrete negative evidence and moving to a bounded target-relative control variable that can act before the hook without attenuating the proven phase request.

The candidate and both required evidence files are now updated. The policy restores the best sampled far-field controller and adds only a `42°` posterior desired-angle envelope, aimed at the repeated near-hard-stop behavior without reintroducing any failed recovery gate. I’m moving through the contract/schema checks now; no CFD will be run.
